small_guidance:
- Add `triton.autotune` over `BLOCK_SP ∈ {32, 64, 128}`, `BLOCK_OC ∈ {32, 64, 128}`, `BLOCK_IC ∈ {16, 32, 64}`, `num_warps ∈ {4, 8}`, `num_stages ∈ {2, 3}` keyed on `(OC, IC, H_out*W_out)` — the current fixed 64/32/16 with num_warps=4 is almost certainly not optimal for the (OC=128, IC=64, ~14²) shape.
- Hoist the IC tile loop to be the outermost loop and accumulate into all four (dh,dw) tiles simultaneously inside one pass over IC — currently the kernel reloads weights and inputs 4×KH×KW times; restructuring to load `x[BLOCK_SP, BLOCK_IC]` once per (h_pre,w_pre) and dot against all kw,kh slices reuses operand registers.
- Replace the `if (dh==0)&(dw==0): acc00 += ...` pattern (which still executes all four IC loops) with four separate explicit `acc_dh_dw` accumulations done inline without redundant work; better: fuse pool into the last reduction by tracking `tl.maximum` of pre-pool tanh outputs in a streaming fashion to halve registers.
large_guidance:
- Switch to an explicit im2col-style GEMM formulation for the transposed-conv: precompute, per output (h_pre,w_pre), the (ic, kh, kw) gather indices and run a single tiled GEMM `[BLOCK_SP_pre, BLOCK_OC] += X_gather[BLOCK_SP_pre, BLOCK_K] @ W[BLOCK_K, BLOCK_OC]` with K = IC·KH·KW. This collapses the 5 nested loops into one K-loop and lets `tl.dot` run at full tensor-core throughput; the 4-pixel pool tile then becomes a 2×2 stride over the pre-pool spatial axis stored in registers and reduced before write.
- Use a channels-last (NHWC) layout for both x and the output buffer so IC loads coalesce along the GEMM-K axis; pre-permute weight to `(KH*KW*IC, OC)` once at init (eval-time constant) and keep it as a contiguous matrix for the inner dot.
- Fuse GroupNorm's first pass (mean/var) into the conv epilogue: have each program emit partial sum and sum-of-squares per (n, group) via `atomic_add` into small scratch tensors, then a tiny second kernel reads scratch, computes inv_std, and applies the affine in-place — eliminates the full re-read of the output tensor that the current standalone GN does twice.
